What it means (plain English): How long the board is, tip of the nose to end of the tail.
How it is measured / options: Feet and inches. Numeric columns use inches.
Why it matters for the AI: Sets paddle power, speed and what waves the board suits.

What it means (plain English): Widest point of the board, measured across the deck.
Why it matters for the AI: More width = more stability and paddle power, less tightness in turns.

What it means (plain English): How thick the board is at its thickest point, usually near the middle.
Why it matters for the AI: Thicker = more float and buoyancy. Thin = more sensitive and responsive.

What it means (plain English): Total space the board takes up, which decides how much it floats.
Why it matters for the AI: The most important number for matching board to surfer weight and skill.

What it means (plain English): Width of the board 12 inches back from the tip of the nose.
Why it matters for the AI: Wider = more paddle power and glide, narrower = a more pointed, performance outline.

What it means (plain English): Width of the board 12 inches in from the end of the tail.
Why it matters for the AI: Wider tail = more speed and lift in small surf. Narrower = more hold and control.

What it means (plain English): How much the nose curves up from a flat surface.
How it is measured / options: Height of the nose tip above a flat surface, in inches.
Why it matters for the AI: More nose rocker = easier steep drops, less speed. Less = faster and flatter.

What it means (plain English): How much the tail curves up from a flat surface.
How it is measured / options: Height of the tail end above a flat surface, in inches.
Why it matters for the AI: More tail rocker = tighter turns, less drive. Less = faster.

What it means (plain English): The location of the board's widest point.
How it is measured / options: Distance from center. Forward = toward the nose, back = toward the tail.
Why it matters for the AI: Forward wide point = more glide. Centered or back = tighter turns.

What it means (plain English): The edges of the board. Full rails are thick and round, thin rails are slim and sharp.
How it is measured / options: Often described as a ratio, e.g. 60/40 or 50/50.
Why it matters for the AI: Full rails float and forgive. Thin, hard rails grip and turn.

What it means (plain English): How sharp the edge is where the bottom meets the rail.
Why it matters for the AI: Harder edge in the tail = more hold and speed. Soft = more forgiving.

What it means (plain English): The shape of the underside of the board.
How it is measured / options: Flat, single concave (a shallow scoop), double concave (two scoops), vee (a roof-shaped ridge).
Why it matters for the AI: Concave adds lift and speed. Vee helps rail-to-rail transitions.

What it means (plain English): The shape of the end of the board.
How it is measured / options: Squash, round, round pin, pin, swallow, rounded square, wing.
Why it matters for the AI: Affects hold, speed and release. Wide tails are looser, pinned tails hold in power.

What it means (plain English): The shape of the tip of the board.
How it is measured / options: Pointed, slightly pointed, rounded, wide rounded.
Why it matters for the AI: Pointed = performance. Wide rounded = glide and stability.

What it means (plain English): How many fins the board has and how they are arranged.
How it is measured / options: Single, twin, twin keel, 2+1, thruster (3), quad (4), 5-fin.
